paper: Hidden Monotonicity: Explaining Deep Neural Networks via their DC Decomposition
audit_scope: Recursive active input closure from arxive/hiddenMonotonicity/main.tex (31 TeX files, including transitive section/appendix tables and figures), compared with all primary thesis tex chapters, figures, tables, and bibliography. verified_findings: HybridDecomposer traces the model with PyTorch FX through GraphAnalyzer and builds decomposition chunks from the traced graph; supported handling is operation/layer-specific, not an unconditional promise for arbitrary PyTorch graphs.

Numerical precision is configurable (float16/float32/float64); the HybridDecomposer default is float32, so the source paper statement that all computations use float64 is not accurate for this pinned implementation.

Activation error caching and gradient caching are configurable; activation assimilation is optional and defaults off, while gradient assimilation is configurable and defaults on in HybridDecomposer. These are corrections/diagnostics against the original model, not unconditionally applied behavior.

The approximation utility create_relu_approximation includes sigmoid, tanh, exp, sqrt, log, reciprocal, GELU, Swish, Mish, and softplus as piecewise-linear ReLU-network approximations over configured ranges. ELU is absent from this utility; nn.ELU is not listed as a split activation in HybridDecomposer._is_activation_operation. The inspected hybrid conversion path does not call the utility, so do not claim the converter generally replaces ELU/Swish activations with ReLU subnetworks.
pinned_implementation_review.recommended_chapter03_paragraph: The pinned implementation uses PyTorch FX to trace a model and organize supported graph operations into decomposition chunks. It provides configurable float16, float32, or float64 arithmetic (float32 by default), activation-error and gradient caches, and optional activation and gradient assimilation against the original model. A separate utility constructs piecewise-linear ReLU-network approximations for selected scalar operations, including GELU, Swish, Mish, sigmoid, tanh, exponential, reciprocal, and softplus over configured ranges; this utility is not called by the inspected hybrid conversion path, and ELU is not among its supported operations. The implementation therefore does not support a general claim that its model converter replaces arbitrary ELU or Swish layers with ReLU subnetworks.
